title: Show HN: Keystroke – open sourcing our internal agents and automations platform
content_html:
Hello HN,

I’m Dallin, building Keystroke with my co-founder Blake. Keystroke is a recent pivot from Buster, our original YC W24 company.

Keystroke lets you build agents and durable workflows as TypeScript in your own repo, then deploy them to a web application where your team can use them. Our repo (ELv2 licensed) is here: https://github.com/keystrokehq/keystroke.

At Buster, we spent a lot of time building internal agents and automations. We used visual platforms like n8n and Zapier, as well as code-first tools like Trigger.dev, Mastra, and several of Vercel’s open frameworks. We genuinely liked many of them, but kept encountering two different problems:

1. Visual platforms gave us integrations, credentials, hosting, and an app the rest of the team could use, but became difficult to test, review, and debug as our systems grew.

2. Code-first tools gave us the flexibility of ordinary TypeScript and worked well with coding agents, but left us building the UI, runtime, permissions, credentials, and operational tooling ourselves.

So, we started building the thing we wish existed: a code-first framework that made it easy to build complex agents and AI systems, with a web app for teams to collaborate on top. We liked it so much that we decided to pivot away from Buster and focus on building Keystroke full time.

With Keystroke, I was able to rebuild our W24 idea (an AI data analyst) in ~5 minutes. I pointed Cursor at our old Buster repo and it was able to:

- spin up a local Keystroke project

- rebuild the OG Buster agent w/ memory, its own file system, etc

- connect our Postgres DB, PostHog, Metabase, and Slack

- build skills for using each of the data sources

- explore our DB and add schema docs to the file system

- build a workflow to keep schema docs synced

- name the agent "Delbert"

- then pushed him up to the Keystroke app

Since then, “Delbert” has been answering ad-hoc questions for me in Slack on a regular basis. He builds me metabase dashboards when I need them. He sets his own triggers, reviews key metrics periodically, and pings me in Slack if anything looks off.

In Keystroke, workflows are ordinary async TypeScript: a `for` loop is an actual `for` loop, inputs use Zod schemas, and everything you build can be tested with Vitest. Our managed runtime makes workflows durable across errors, sleeps, approval steps, and process restarts.

Agents wrap Vercel’s AI SDK and can use workflows, actions, other agents, MCP servers, and integrations as tools. They also include memory, a persistent filesystem, web search, triggers, and optional VM sandboxes.

Deployed agents and workflows instantly appear in the web app with a chat UI, workflow visualizations, input forms, sharing, credential management, integrations, and logs.

The entire platform was built from the ground up with coding agents in mind. Your coding agent can use the CLI to scaffold a local directory with a Keystroke project and an AGENTS.md. Then, it can build whatever agent or AI system you want, search our docs, run tests, and push what you build up to the Keystroke platform.

We plan to make money from our cloud offering, which has a free plan and usage-based pricing.

Our docs are here: https://keystroke.ai/docs.

You can watch a quick demo of Keystroke here: https://supercut.ai/share/keystroke/zeor1pD0bNlSTOuLUWmRBT?v....

You can try on cloud for free at: https://keystroke.ai/.

We’d especially appreciate feedback from people who have maintained agents and AI systems in visual tools or code-first frameworks. Where does this approach seem useful, and where are we rebuilding something that already works well elsewhere?

blocks.html_en: Deployed agents and workflows instantly appear in the web app with a chat UI, workflow visualizations, input forms, sharing, credential management, integrations, and logs.

blocks.html_en: The entire platform was built from the ground up with coding agents in mind. Your coding agent can use the CLI to scaffold a local directory with a Keystroke project and an AGENTS.md. Then, it can build whatever agent or AI system you want, search our docs, run tests, and push what you build up to the Keystroke platform.

content_html_zh: 你好 HN，我是 Dallin，正在与我的联合创始人 Blake 一起构建 Keytrip。 KeyStroke 是 Buster（我们最初的 YC W24 公司）最近的一个支点。Key Strike 允许您在自己的存储库中以 TypeScript 的形式构建代理和持久工作流程，然后将它们部署到 Web 应用程序，您的团队可以在其中使用它们。 我们的存储库（ELv2 许可）位于：https://github.com/keyrinklehq/keyrinkle。在 Buster，我们花了很多时间构建内部代理和自动化。 我们使用了 n8n 和 Zapier 等可视化平台，以及 Trigger.dev、Mastra 等代码优先工具以及 Vercel 的几个开放框架。 我们真的很喜欢其中的许多，但不断遇到两个不同的问题：1。 可视化平台为我们提供了集成、凭证、托管和团队其他成员可以使用的应用程序，但随着我们系统的增长，测试、审查和调试变得困难。2。 代码优先工具为我们提供了普通 TypeScript 的灵活性，并且与编码代理配合良好，但让我们自己构建 UI、运行时、权限、凭证和操作工具。因此，我们开始构建我们希望存在的东西：一个代码优先框架，可以轻松构建复杂的代理和 AI 系统，并提供一个供团队在其上协作的 Web 应用程序。 我们非常喜欢它，因此我们决定放弃 Buster，专注于全职构建 Key Strike。通过 Keyrinkle，我能够在大约 5 分钟内重建我们的 W24 想法（人工智能数据分析师）。 我将 Cursor 指向我们的旧 Buster 存储库，它能够： - 启动本地 Key Strike 项目 - 重建带有内存、其自己的文件系统等的 OG Buster 代理 - 连接我们的 Postgres DB、PostHog、Metabase 和 Slack - 构建使用每个数据源的技能 - 探索我们的数据库并将架构文档添加到文件系统 - 构建一个工作流程以保持架构文档同步 - 将代理命名为“Delbert” - 然后将其推送到 Key Strike 应用程序然后，“Delbert”就一直在 Slack 中定期回答我的临时问题。 当我需要时，他为我构建元数据库仪表板。 他设置自己的触发器，定期检查关键指标，如果有任何问题，就会在 Slack 中向我发送 ping 消息。在 Keyrinkle 中，工作流程是普通的异步 TypeScript：“for”循环是实际的“for”循环，输入使用 Zod 模式，并且您构建的所有内容都可以使用 Vitest 进行测试。 我们的托管运行时使工作流程在错误、睡眠、批准步骤和流程重新启动方面具有持久性。代理封装了 Vercel 的 AI SDK，并且可以使用工作流程、操作、其他代理、MCP 服务器和集成作为工具。 它们还包括内存、持久文件系统、Web 搜索、触发器和可选的 VM 沙箱。部署的代理和工作流会立即出现在 Web 应用程序中，并带有聊天 UI、工作流可视化、输入表单、共享、凭证管理、集成和日志。整个平台是从头开始构建的，考虑到了编码代理。 您的编码代理可以使用 CLI 来构建包含 Key Strike 项目和 AGENTS.md 的本地目录。 然后，它可以构建您想要的任何代理或人工智能系统，搜索我们的文档，运行测试，并将您构建的内容推送到 Keyrinkle 平台。我们计划从我们的云产品中赚钱，该产品有免费计划和基于使用的定价。我们的文档在这里：https://keyrinkle.ai/docs。您可以在这里观看 Keyrinkle 的快速演示：https://supercut.ai/share/keyrinkle/zeor1pD0bNlSTOuLUWmRBT?v....您可以在云上尝试免费：https://keylines.ai/。我们特别感谢那些在视觉工具或代码优先框架中维护代理和人工智能系统的人的反馈。 这种方法在哪里看起来有用，我们在哪里重建已经在其他地方运行良好的东西？
